messages:
megan.lee: perf-bot flagged a spike in p99 for gpt-slim-v2 on dedi-pool-eu-west :rotating_light:
perf-bot: ALERT: /models/gpt-slim-v2/latency_p99 > 700ms (dedi-pool-eu-west) at 2026-03-05T14:03:21Z
megan.lee: reports from a customer about interactive responses being slow. grabbing traces would help.
ricardo: got scheduler logs and a microtrace. pattern: dramatic jump in single-request dispatches starting ~14:00 UTC. continuous batching pack sizes collapsed.
ricardo: batch histogram:
```
continuous_batching_batch_size_histogram{le="1"}  28911
continuous_batching_batch_size_histogram{le="2"}  40222
continuous_batching_batch_size_histogram{le="4"}  41000
continuous_batching_batch_size_histogram{le="8"}  41280
```
ricardo: target pack is 8 but effective packing is almost all singletons.
Tom_h: KV eviction spikes on nodes dedi-eu-12 and dedi-eu-15 around 14:01
```
kv_cache_evictions_total{node="dedi-eu-12"}  512
kv_cache_hits_total{node="dedi-eu-12"}       2090
```
anita_g: KV churn + small microbatches = extra latency (tokenizer warm start + kv transfer). Also saw kernel fallback to quantized-kernel-2 which has a higher setup for short sequences.
james: there was a long historical training-style job (tag=long-context) scheduled across some of these hosts at 13:58. admission should have isolated it but we shipped an admission refactor in PR #4710 last week.
megan.lee: PR #4710 touched admission heuristics and kernel fallback ordering? anyone recall specifics?
ricardo: yes. it added a kernel-matching pass and modified admission scoring to bias toward lowest-latency kernels; unfortunately the metric used ignored packability, so high-scoring long jobs were admitted sooner, starving pack windows.
ricardo: excerpt from scheduler debug at 14:02:09:
```
[admission] req id=abc123 ctx=32 tags=[interactive] score=9 pack_score=1 -> queued
[admission] req id=def456 ctx=4096 tags=[long-context] score=13 pack_score=0 -> admit immediate
[packing] attempt_target=8 actual=1 reason="pack window expired"
```
anita_g: kernel selector also fell back to quantized-kernel-2 when memory was low; that kernel has a per-dispatch init cost that hurts tiny microbatches.
james: TL;DR: we have a packing priority regression + kernel fallback extra overhead + KV eviction from noisy long job.
megan.lee: quick mitigations:
- revert admission scoring change on canaries
- pin interactive slices to fp16-kernel-stable on affected pool
- apply temporary placement rule to limit tag=long-context concurrency per node
ricardo: applied placement rule reduction for long-context on dedi-eu-12 and dedi-eu-15 now.
ricardo: PATCH sent:
```
POST /internal/scheduler/rules
{"rules": [{"tag":"long-context","max_per_node":1}]}
```
Tom_h: rolling kernel pin to fp16-kernel-stable on canaries now.
megan.lee: rolling back admission change on canaries too. monitor batch histograms.
ricardo: after rollback on canary nodes (14:10), immediate improvements:
```
before: p99=780ms p50=95ms
after:  p99=310ms p50=90ms
continuous_batching_batch_size_histogram{le="1"} dropped ~60%
```
perf-bot: METRIC: /models/gpt-slim-v2/latency_p99 dropped to 320ms on canary at 2026-03-05T14:12:40Z
megan.lee: did KV evictions fall after placement rule?
Tom_h: yes, dedi-eu-12 evictions 512 -> 38 within 6m.
anita_g: next steps: add synthetic perf test that runs interleaved small interactive requests with a long job to catch regressions, add packability unit test to admission scoring.
james: action items:
- megan: write incident note + timeline, include traces and config diffs
- ricardo: change admission scoring to include pack_score as a first-class factor and add unit tests
- tom: adjust kernel selector to prefer fp16 for seq_len <= 128 and add perf gate for kernel swaps
- anita: add kv_cache_eviction alert with threshold and 5m burn-in to catch noisy neighbors
megan.lee: leaving placement throttle for 12h while we validate. objections?
james: +1
Tom_h: +1
anita_g: +1
ricardo: +1
megan.lee: thanks all. posting full incident in #incidents and scheduling a deep-dive at 16:00 UTC.
perf-bot: INCIDENT: tail-latency degradation on dedi-pool-eu-west mitigated (owner: megan.lee) at 2026-03-05T14:22:00Z
megan.lee: saved traces: s3://redwood-internal/perf/2026-03-05/gpt-slim-v2/trace-14-00.json
megan.lee: summary: regression introduced in admission heuristic + kernel fallback behavior + KV cache eviction due to noisy long-context jobs => p99 spike. mitigated via rollback, kernel pin, and placement rules. permanent fixes planned.
